task_message:
Case F26: segment the fibrous soft-tissue tumor on this T2-weighted MRI.

Volume: 271x271x265 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.
final_assistant_text:
Case F26 is complete.

**Result:** The fibrous soft-tissue tumor was segmented as a single 72.7 mL, one-component mask spanning axial slices 72–140, coronal 111–170, and sagittal 150–196.

**Approach:**
1. **Localization:** Scanned the volume with axial/coronal/sagittal contact sheets and identified the markedly T2-hyperintense, lobulated soft-tissue mass at the anterolateral aspect of the limb (greatest cross-section around axial slice ~100).
2. **Initial mask:** Placed three positive points in the bright mass core (marks 514, 490, 540) on axial slice 101, yielding a 73.6 mL mask.
3. **Verification:** Checked the boundary in all three planes (axials 76–134, coronals 126–166, sagittals 162–186) and the past-the-mask end slices. The mask follows the lobulated hyperintense mass, with the bright peripheral crescent and surrounding tissue judged to be subcutaneous fat/skin, and the dependent bright structure below the limb judged gel/support material.
4. **Refinement:** Ran a model boundary refinement, which only slightly adjusted the outline (−2.3/+1.4 mL) and kept the same coherent shape; the automatic candidate proposals (surrounding fat, skin, and distant bright vessels) were rejected as non-lesion tissue.

**Confidence: medium** — the mass core and its lobulated margin are clearly and completely outlined in all three planes; the only uncertainty is at the feathery perilesional edema/skin-fat interface where the tumor margin fades.
